title: Professional Life
description: Work told as a life rather than as a job description: a businesswoman of the year looking back on the years she left a two-year-old with a childminder, a deaf woman who teaches music to three hundred children, and two Norwegian students in Japan saying what they want to become and why; the words of working life (a manager, a deficit against a profit, a childminder, to drop somebody and to pick somebody up as the two ends of the same day, to look after, to be fond of, self-sufficient, relieved, guilty, to settle down); should have plus past participle for a regret met inside a text instead of inside an exercise, and would plus base verb for a habit that is over, told apart from a conditional by the presence of an if and from a simple past by the stretch of time behind it; the three expressions of purpose printed in the grammar summary of page 117 - to plus verb, in order to plus verb, and so that plus a whole clause carrying one of eight modals - with the subject test that decides between them and the two errors that cost marks every year; the three sounds of the final -s and the rule of the vibrating throat that produces them without a list to learn; used to plus base verb, its meaning of not any more, its three forms and the d that disappears after did; the vocabulary of qualifications (a degree, a physician who is a doctor and not a physicist, surgery, a check-up, stitches, an internship, competitive, to earn, training) and of Emma's story (partially, deafness, a hearing aid, fed up, hooked, pitch, a scholarship, drama, to set up, worthwhile); and step 1 of the career research project, the narrative report of an ideal job
